content: Ritonavir interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through the CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 pathways, as well as the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels and effects, necessitating careful monitoring and dose adjustments in many cases. Below are the key interactions: 1. Progesterone (intravaginal gel, micronized, or natural): Ritonavir increases progesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Propranolol: Ritonavir increases propranolol levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 3. Quercetin: Quercetin decreases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 4. Quetiapine: Ritonavir increases quetiapine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity through QTc interval prolongation. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs and monitor patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. 5. Quinidine: Ritonavir increases quinidine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: These drugs increase ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Quizartinib: Ritonavir increases quizartinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 8. Ranolazine: Ranolazine increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 9. Repaglinide: Ritonavir increases repaglinide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Ribociclib: Ribociclib increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 11. Rifabutin: Ritonavir increases rifabutin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifaximin: Ritonavir increases rifaximin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 15. Rilpivirine: Ritonavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity through QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and avoid co-administration with drugs that prolong QT or in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. 16. Ripretinib: Ritonavir increases ripretinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Risperidone: Ritonavir increases risperidone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 18. Roflumilast (oral and topical): Ritonavir decreases oral roflumilast levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism but increases topical roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 19. Rolapitant: Rolapitant increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates may remain elevated for at least 28 days after rolapitant administration. Use caution and monitor. 20. Romidepsin: Ritonavir increases romidepsin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 21. Rosiglitazone: Ritonavir decreases rosiglitazone effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 22. Rosuvastatin: Ritonavir increases rosuvastatin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 24. Rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Sacubitril/Valsartan: Ritonavir increases sacubitril/valsartan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. 26. Sarecycline: Sarecycline increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities and consider dosage reduction. 27. Saxagliptin: Ritonavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 28. Seladelpar: Ritonavir increases seladelpar levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A inhibitors. 29. Sertraline: Ritonavir increases sertraline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 30. Silodosin: Ritonavir increases silodosin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Sirolimus: Ritonavir increases sirolimus levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 32. Sitagliptin: Ritonavir decreases sitagliptin effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 33. Solifenacin: Ritonavir increases solifenacin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Sorafenib: Ritonavir increases sorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 36. Stiripentol: Stiripentol increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 37. Streptomycin: Ritonavir increases streptomycin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 38. Sufentanil SL: Ritonavir increases sufentanil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. 39. Sunitinib: Ritonavir increases sunitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Tacrolimus (oral and ointment): Ritonavir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 41. Talazoparib: Ritonavir increases talazoparib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 42. Tamoxifen: Ritonavir decreases tamoxifen metabolism to its active metabolites, potentially leading to poor clinical outcomes. Use caution and monitor. 43. Tamsulosin: Ritonavir increases tamsulosin levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Tasimelteon: Ritonavir increases tasimelteon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Tazemetostat: Ritonavir decreases tazemetostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Temsirolimus: Ritonavir increases temsirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Teniposide: Ritonavir increases teniposide levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Tenofovir DF: Ritonavir increases tenofovir levels by decreasing its elimination, increasing the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 50. Terbinafine: Ritonavir increases terbinafine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 51. Tetrabenazine: Ritonavir increases tetrabenazine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Reduce tetrabenazine dose by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 52. Tezacaftor: Ritonavir increases tezacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 53. Theophylline: Ritonavir increases theophylline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Tiagabine: Ritonavir increases tiagabine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Ticagrelor: Ritonavir increases ticagrelor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 56. Timolol: Ritonavir increases timolol levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, and AV block. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 57. Tinidazole: Ritonavir increases tinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Tipranavir: Ritonavir increases tipranavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 59. Tisotumab vedotin: Ritonavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Tobramycin: Ritonavir increases tobramycin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 61. Tolterodine: Ritonavir increases tolterodine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Tolvaptan: Ritonavir increases tolvaptan levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 63. Topiramate: Topiramate decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 64. Toremifene: Ritonavir increases toremifene levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Tramadol: Ritonavir increases tramadol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome. Adjust dose as needed. 66. Trazodone: Ritonavir increases trazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 67. Triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension: Ritonavir increases triamcinolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 68. Triazolam: Ritonavir increases triazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 69. Trimipramine: Ritonavir increases trimipramine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 70. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 71. Ublituximab: Ublituximab decreases ritonavir effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 72. Ubrogepant: Ritonavir decreases ubrogepant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 73. Ulipristal: Ritonavir increases ulipristal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 74. Umeclidinium bromide/Vilanterol inhaled: Ritonavir increases levels of these drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 75. Upadacitinib: Ritonavir increases upadacitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 76. Valbenazine: Ritonavir increases valbenazine levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 77. Valsartan: Ritonavir increases valsartan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. 78. Vamorolone: Ritonavir increases vamorolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 79. Vardenafil: Ritonavir increases vardenafil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 80. Vemurafenib: Ritonavir increases vemurafenib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 81. Venlafaxine: Ritonavir increases venlafaxine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 82. Verapamil: Ritonavir increases verapamil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 83. Viloxazine: Viloxazine increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 84. Vinblastine: Ritonavir increases vinblastine levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 85. Vincristine: Ritonavir increases vincristine levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 86. Voclosporin: Ritonavir and voclosporin may increase each other's effects through QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 87. Warfarin: Ritonavir decreases warfarin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 88. Zafirlukast: Zafirlukast increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 89. Zanubrutinib: Ritonavir increases zanubrutinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 90. Zidovudine: Ritonavir and zidovudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 91. Zileuton: Ritonavir increases zileuton levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 92. Zuranolone: Ritonavir increases zuranolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 93. Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 94. Alfentanil: Ritonavir increases alfentanil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 95. Aliskiren: Ritonavir increases aliskiren levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Significance unknown. 96. Alosetron: Ritonavir increases alosetron levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 97. Alvimopan: Ritonavir increases alvimopan levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Significance unknown. 98. Amphetamine: Ritonavir increases amphetamine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 99. Anastrozole: Anastrozole increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 100. Aripiprazole: Ritonavir increases aripiprazole levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 101. Armodafinil: Ritonavir increases armodafinil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Significance unknown. 102. Atazanavir: Ritonavir increases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 103. Bosentan: Ritonavir increases bosentan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 104. Cevimeline: Ritonavir increases cevimeline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 105. Chlorpromazine: Ritonavir increases chlorpromazine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 106. Clarithromycin: Ritonavir increases clarithromycin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 107. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 108. Dapsone: Ritonavir increases dapsone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 109. Dexfenfluramine: Ritonavir increases dexfenfluramine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 110. Dextroamphetamine: Ritonavir increases dextroamphetamine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 111. Dextromethorphan: Ritonavir increases dextromethorphan levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 112. Disopyramide: Ritonavir increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 113. Docetaxel: Ritonavir increases docetaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 114. Donepezil: Ritonavir increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 115. Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 116. Dutasteride: Ritonavir increases dutasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 117. Efavirenz: Ritonavir increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 118. Encainide: Ritonavir increases encainide levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. 119. Eplerenone: Ritonavir increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 120. Eucalyptus: Ritonavir increases eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significance unknown. 121. Fesoterodine: Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Significance unknown. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when ritonavir is co-administered with other medications.
